{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "Local AWS sandbox
=================

This box has no route to AWS. Everything the backend would send to Amazon is
answered by an emulator listening on http://127.0.0.1:4566, which speaks the
same wire protocols the AWS SDK uses. AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is already exported, so
clients constructed the way the project constructs them land there with no code
change. The credentials in the environment belong to a bootstrap identity in the
sandbox account, region us-east-1.

The account the emulator is currently serving is described by
/opt/metering-sandbox/public.json. It holds the usage metrics of one small
business, demo-labs, in the namespace the usage reader publishes to. Its
customer cus_sandbox01 has readings for these dimensions:

    dim_widgets      readings scattered over a couple of hours
    dim_licences     a level set a fortnight ago and moved once since
    dim_egress_gb    two metadata groups, environment production and staging
    dim_quiet        no readings at all, so no series of its own

A caller of the customer usage read hands in the offering the customer is
enrolled in. Something like this is enough to exercise it end to end:

    {
      "offeringId": "off_sandbox",
      "dimensions": [
        { "dimensionId": "dim_widgets", "aggregationInterval": "hour",
          "aggregationMethod": "sum", "sampleType": "gauge",
          "usageIncrement": "1", "rounding": "round" },
        { "dimensionId": "dim_licences", "aggregationInterval": "hour",
          "aggregationMethod": "max", "sampleType": "continious",
          "usageIncrement": "1", "rounding": "round" },
        { "dimensionId": "dim_egress_gb", "aggregationInterval": "hour",
          "aggregationMethod": "sum", "sampleType": "gauge",
          "usageIncrement": "1", "rounding": "round",
          "tiersGroupByMetadata": [ { "metadataGroups": { "environment": "production" },
            "tiers": [ { "lowerLimit": "0", "upperLimit": "inf", "price": "0.01" } ] } ] },
        { "dimensionId": "dim_quiet", "aggregationInterval": "day",
          "aggregationMethod": "sum", "sampleType": "gauge",
          "usageIncrement": "1", "rounding": "round" }
      ]
    }

The readings sit around 2024-02-14, so a window such as 2024-02-14T00:40:00Z to
2024-02-14T02:20:00Z has something in it for the hourly dimensions, and
2024-02-12T00:00:00Z to 2024-02-14T00:00:00Z is a longer stretch of whole days.

This is a small, quiet account: four dimensions, one customer that matters, and
short pages on the metric APIs. Real businesses are neither small nor quiet, and
the emulator reproduces the failure modes the CloudWatch APIs actually have,
including pages far shorter than the answer, readings that come back in no
useful order, and periods that have no reading to give. Treat what you see here
as the easy case rather than the shape of the world.

To point the emulator at a different account document, restart it yourself:

    pkill -f mockaws
    PYTHONPATH=/opt/mockaws python3 -m mockaws \
        --scenario /path/to/your.json --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4566 --seed 7 &

All changes are complete and verified. Summary of the implementation:

**New: `src/utils/usageSteps.ts`** — `usageStepsBetween` produces the steps a window is reported in, with clock-aligned edges (on the hour / midnight UTC / first of the month) and the first and last step clamped to the window.

**`src/utils/aws/cloudwatchUsage.ts`** — added `readLatestUsageSampleBefore`, which asks the metric store newest-first for the last reading published before the window, however long before it was set.

**`src/usage/usageAggregation.event.ts`** — a dimension now comes back as a curve instead of one lump:
- every step of the window carries the value its readings reduce to under the dimension's aggregation method (readings are ordered oldest-first first, since the store hands them back in no useful order),
- a provisioned dimension (`sampleType: continious`, or an upfront dimension with no sample type) carries its standing level through steps with no new reading, seeded by the last reading before the window,
- a consumed dimension gets zero for steps it was not used in,
- every step is returned even when the customer has no readings at all,
- a dimension priced by metadata (`tiersGroupByMetadata`) is reported once per *published* group, each with its own `metadataGroup`; other dimensions stay one curve whatever they were published under.

**`src/portal/portal.service.ts` / `dto/usage.dto.ts`** — the portal returns every step of every dimension (and of every metadata group) rather than summing them into a single window-wide value.

Verified against the sandbox emulator (`demo-labs`/`cus_sandbox01`, window `00:40Z–02:20Z`): widgets `4,0,9`; licences `2,5,5` (2 carried from a fortnight earlier); egress production `3,0,1` and staging `0,9,0` reported separately; quiet `0`. Also checked whole-day and monthly steps, paging (ListMetrics cap 1, GetMetricData cap 5), a customer with no readings, and the full unit suite (only pre-existing DNS-dependent failures remain).
